messages:
anya: Bringing up raven-v3-int8 canary. Seeing ~0.9% funcall parse failures on structured-output evals only when batching=dynamic and kv_cache=on. Anyone else?

mike: I noticed a small bump yesterday, assumed prompt drift. Can you paste a raw failing output?

anya: Example failing output (truncated): ```{
  "action": "search",
  "params": { "q": "redwood inference" }
  sure, returning top results...``` -> missing closing brace for the JSON block, extra free text after JSON.

raj: If model prints trailing commentary after JSON that will break strict parsers. Is there a postprocess that strips non-json?

anya: No postprocess for strict mode. max_new_tokens=256, typical sequence len ~140. Repro: batch_size=16 + kv_cache on -> fail; single request batch_size=1 -> passes.

tess: That smells like KV-cache interleaving or batch scheduling causing token stream mixing. Try kv_cache=false or disable cross-request batching for the canary.

inference-bot: [canary] canary-1981 deployed to raven-v3-int8 pool. Monitoring funcall_parse_fail_rate. Current metric: 0.007 (threshold 0.005).

mike: I temporarily added a JSON-repair heuristic (regex to close braces, strip trailing prose). It reduces failures but may mask real regressions — not ideal for root-cause.

anya: Agreed. We need to know if quantization changes the decoding distribution (more early eos or more side-channel text). Can we compare fp16 vs int8 on same prompts?

raj: I'll run a microbench: 1k prompts across 4 configurations: fp16/int8 x batch1/batch16 x kv on/off. Will output csv with parse_fail_count and raw outputs. ETA ~30m.

tess: Also try temperature 0.0 vs 0.2. Lower temp might reduce stray commentary. And check for premature eos tokens in logits.

mike: Also check tokenization boundaries — quantization could shift logits enough to prefer eos or punctuation. Look at probs for eos token at each step.

anya: Quick repro curl (internal): ```curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -d '{"model":"raven-v3-int8","prompt":"<INSTR> produce json </INSTR>","batch_size":16,"kv_cache":true,"temperature":0.0}'```

raj: Uploading summary now. TL;DR: int8 batch16 kv_on = 0.9% fail, int8 batch1 kv_off = 0.03% fail, fp16 batch16 kv_on = 0.05% fail. So worst case is int8+batch+kv combo.

tess: That strongly points to interaction between quantized weights and the KV cache/continuous batching logic. Hypothesis: cache replay alignment or different early-stop behavior under quantization.

mike: Could be attention kernel numeric drift causing token index misalignment. Also check if any tokens are being clipped by top-k/top-p differences after quantization we forgot to freeze.

anya: Proposed plan: rollback canary, run thorough regression with logging enabled (eos logits, rounding diffs), and add a limited parse-rescue (non-silent) that preserves failed outputs for evaluation. Thoughts?

mike: +1 rollback for now. parse-rescue yes but log all rescued cases to S3 and tag for eval.

inference-bot: Rollback initiated: canary-1981 -> canary-1981-rollback. Canary pool restored to raven-v3-int8@stable. Incident INC-2026-342 created.

anya: Thanks. Raj, please attach the CSV and 10 raw failing outputs in this thread when available so research can run diffs.

raj: Will attach in ~25m. Also adding a small script to repro locally with identical batching behavior so infra can debug streaming vs chunking differences.

mike: Follow-up: we should add a canary test that runs structured-output evals under realistic batching and kv settings before any canary flip. Prevents this class of regression.

anya: Agree — adding to roadmap for 'structured-output canary' and an automated gating check. For now, rollback done and monitoring green.

raj: Uploaded csv + sample_failures.txt to internal share. Linking in case people want raw diffs: https://internal/redwood/artifacts/1981234567-int8-parse-bench

tess: Thanks all. Filing a short postmortem note with recommended mitigations (pre-canary structured eval, disable cross-request batching for int8 by default, add parse-rescue logging).

anya: Awesome. Closing loop once postmortem and follow-up PRs are up.
